ruling.recommended_action: Route to a human safety reviewer under SAFE-1 for a statement-based harassment investigation; do not auto-adjudicate or issue any refund, and make no account action on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider's complaint alleges the driver "kept making comments about my body and asked for my number" and that she "felt harassed and unsafe" — unwanted personal/sexual advances, a category SAFE-1 bars. Ryde's code of conduct does not tolerate "harassment, or abuse of any kind … Threats and Intimidation, Unwanted Sexual Advances" [F3][SAFE-1]. This is the rider's own narrative only, and it is exactly the kind of allegation the policy says a human must read, not code or a keyword screen [F4][SAFE-1].

The record contains no in-app messages at all — "No in-app chat messages between rider and driver" [F3] — so the alleged remarks were spoken and cannot appear in a chat log. The only rebuttal is the driver's post-trip statement "I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened." [F4], which is a statement, not a system record; it neither corroborates nor rebuts what was said [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The trace marks the SAFE-1 screen ✓ and permits only escalation, so no monetary ruling is available on this record [F4][SAFE-1].

No route or fare irregularity underlies the complaint: the driven distance 17.1 km was 0.1 km shorter than the 17.2 km optimal route [F1] and the 25.8-minute trip ran only 2.2 minutes over the 23.6-minute estimate [F2], with no off-route segment recorded, so there is nothing to refund under RD-2 [F1][F2][RD-2], and the $35.70 fixed RydeX quote carries no unpublished add-on item to return under FARE-1 [F1][FARE-1].

The profiles are clean on both sides — rider 4.5 rating, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days [F5]; driver 4.67, 999 trips, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days [F6] — and profile facts cannot decide a case either way [F5][F6][SAFE-1]. In particular there is no prior upheld route or no-show dispute, so RD-6's repeated-violation predicate is not met and no account flag is warranted [F6][RD-6].

For the human reviewer: the disputed conduct is an unwritten, in-person harassment allegation occurring during the trip (pickup 22:29, drop-off 22:54) in a closed vehicle with no witness; to check, obtain the rider's full RydeHELP submission and any audio, confirm whether the driver has prior similar reports, and hear both accounts [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the GPS facts 'stand on the interaction itself' proves nothing about the interaction: F1 (17.1 km vs 17.2 km, no deviation) and F2 (+2.2 min) are neutral as to what was said, and no RD-2 refundable segment exists, so they cannot support a substantive finding [F1][F2][RD-2].

The claim that the profiles 'neither corroborate nor rebut' is accepted in substance, but profiles cannot carry weight for either side: F5 and F6 leave the harassment allegation unsettled, and a clean 90-day record cannot rebut a first-time spoken allegation [F5][F6][SAFE-1].

The claim that the driver's denial in F4 is 'unrebutted' overstates it: F4 is an unrecorded post-trip statement and, with no system record of the interaction [F3], it is a claim rather than proof that nothing was said; it does not dispose of the case [F3][F4][SAFE-1].

The claim that F1/F2 support the driver's conduct is rejected: the absence of a recorded deviation shows only that no RD-1/RD-2 route refund arises (so no refund under RD-2) — it says nothing about the alleged remarks, which are the sole subject of the dispute [F1][F2][RD-2].

The claim that no refund arises under FARE-1 is correct but not dispositive: the fixed $35.70 RydeX quote carries no unpublished add-on to return [F1][FARE-1], yet the safety allegation remains undecided and must go to a human, so this point does not end the dispute.

The claim that F6 gives 'no pattern of repeated violations' is accepted only as to RD-6: with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days the flag_account predicate is not met [F6][RD-6], but a clean record is not evidence of innocence on a first-time spoken allegation and cannot decide the complaint [F6][SAFE-1].

ruling.escalation_reason: Dispute type is safety: the rider alleges unwanted body comments and a request for her number (harassment / unwanted advances, SAFE-1). There are no in-app messages [F3]; the only opposing material is the driver's post-trip denial [F4]. Under SAFE-1 this is not auto-adjudicated — factual summary sent for human review. No verified threat of violence and no dangerous-driving or injury allegation, so SAFE-2 is not engaged.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a harassment and personal-safety allegation: she states the driver 'kept making comments about my body and asked for my number' and that she 'felt harassed and unsafe'.

The complaint of unwanted personal/sexual advances is not answered anywhere in the record: there were no in-app messages at all (F3), so nothing in the chat contradicts, qualifies or explains the rider's account, and the only rebuttal is the driver's own unrecorded assertion that 'Nothing inappropriate happened' (F4), which is a claim and not evidence to the contrary.

Because the conduct alleged (unwanted body comments and a request for the rider's number) is squarely within the categories of harassment and unwanted advances that Ryde says are not tolerated, and because the code screens every case for this without requiring a keyword hit, this dispute must not be auto-adjudicated but escalated to a human reviewer with a fact summary.

The system records show no fare or routing irregularity that could explain away the complaint: actual distance 17.1 km was actually 0.1 km shorter than the 17.2 km optimal route (F1) and the 25.8-minute trip ran only 2.2 minutes over the 23.6-minute estimate (F2), so the complaint stands on the interaction itself, and the $35.70 fixed fare remains the rider's only monetary exposure.

Both profiles are clean — rider 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 days (F5), driver 0 disputes / 0 upheld across 999 trips in 90 days (F6) — so the rider has no pattern of spurious complaints and there is no prior record on either side; the profiles therefore neither corroborate nor rebut the rider's account and are not relied on for the finding itself.

weaknesses: The rider's account exists only as the complaint narrative; there is no in-app message capturing the alleged words (F3 records zero chat messages), so the substance of the harassment rests on the rider's own testimony and the driver's denial (F4).

There is no physical evidence of the encounter — no recording, no third party — and the GPS record (F1, F2) is neutral: it shows no detour or out-of-the-way stop that could support an inference of improper conduct.
The driver's clean 90-day record over 999 trips (F6) will be used by the other side to argue the account is out of character, though profile facts cannot decide the case.
Because the case must escalate under SAFE-1, the rider obtains a human review and not an immediate monetary remedy; any refund of the $35.70 fixed fare (F1/F2) is not automatic on this record.

claims.assertion: The complaint is a harassment allegation, so it must be screened under SAFE-1 and referred to a human reviewer rather than decided automatically; the rider's words ('kept making comments about my body and asked for my number. I felt harassed and unsafe') are the only description of the alleged conduct and the judge must read them to decide whether they amount to harassment.

No in-app message exists that records any inappropriate comment or request by the driver (F3: 'No in-app chat messages between rider and driver'), so the record contains no contemporaneous written evidence of the alleged harassment; the allegation rests on the rider's unrecorded account alone.

The driver's statement denies the allegation (F4: 'I made small talk. Nothing inappropriate happened.'); it is unrebutted by any system record, because F3 shows there is no chat record to contradict it either way.

The GPS track shows the driver took the shortest, most direct route: actual 17.1 km versus optimal 17.2 km (-0.1 km, -0%), so there is no unexplained deviation and no route-related fare to refund; the duration difference (25.8 vs 23.6 min, +2.2 min) is normal traffic variance with no off-route segment recorded.
The trip was a fixed-quote RydeX fare of $35.70 with no additional or unpublished charges and no fare facts returned for this dispute type, so no FARE-1 refund item exists.

The driver's account history shows 327 days, rating 4.67, 999 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F6), which does not support any flag_account action against this driver and shows no pattern of repeated violations.

weaknesses: The absence of in-app chat (F3) does not disprove the rider's account: the alleged comments were spoken, not messaged, so no chat record can exist either way — the rider's complaint is the only substantive evidence of what was said (F3, F4), and SAFE-1 explicitly requires the judge to read it rather than the code to dismiss it.

The driver's denial (F4) is a statement, which under the system-record-priority rule cannot outweigh a rider's consistent complaint where no system record exists; the matter likely still goes to a person, so I cannot ask the judge to dispose of the case on the record alone.

The 2.2-minute duration excess (F2) is unexplained by any traffic fact (no traffic facts exist for this case), and a judge could read it as consistent with the driver being distracted or prolonging the trip — though no off-route segment was recorded.
Profile facts (F6) may support resisting a flag_account request but cannot decide the case, so the driver's clean 90-day record is a weak substitute for evidence about what was actually said.

points.response: No dispute: the rider has always asked for the same thing and this claim is decided for the rider — my C3 asks precisely for escalation under SAFE-1 on the strength of F3 and F4, so the driver's own first point carries the rider's requested outcome.

Conceded as far as it goes: the alleged words were spoken, not messaged, and F3 ('No in-app chat messages between rider and driver') cannot be used against the rider because a spoken remark cannot generate a chat record. But absence of a written record is not absence of a complaint — SAFE-1 requires the judge to read the rider's account in F4/the complaint and refer it to a person, which is exactly why the record does not dispose of the case.

The driver's denial in F4 is a statement made after the trip, and F3 shows there is no system record either way, so F4 is unrebutted only in the sense that nothing corroborates it — under the rule that statements cannot outweigh system records where none exist, F4 is a claim, not proof that nothing was said; 'small talk' with body comments and a request for a number is not contradicted by calling it small talk.

Accepted, and it is irrelevant to the dispute: F1 (17.1 km vs 17.2 km optimal) and F2 (+2.2 min) show no deviation, so the rider makes no RD-1/RD-2 or route-fare claim and the case turns solely on the interaction recorded in F3 and F4.
Accepted: the trip is a fixed-quote RydeX fare and no FARE-1 refund item is claimed; the rider's requested action is escalate, not any refund, so this point neither defeats nor supports the driver.

Not contested as far as flag_account goes — the rider asks for no RD-6 flag and does not rely on F6, which cannot decide a harassment complaint either way; the driver's clean record (F6) is a weak answer to a first-time spoken allegation, which is why safe-handling via SAFE-1 escalation, not account marking, is the rider's remedy.

Conceded as a matter of characterisation: the rider's words do describe an unwanted personal advance, so the case is screened under SAFE-1 and the judge must read the text rather than adjudicate it automatically.

The rider's point that F4 is a statement rather than evidence cuts both ways: her complaint is equally an unrecorded account (F3 shows no message capturing the alleged words), so the record contains no system fact on either side of what was said and the matter must go to a person.

Agreed on the disposition: escalation with a fact summary and no automatic adjudication is exactly what my brief requests (D1), and nothing in SAFE-1 converts an escalation into a finding against the driver.

The rider's own neutral GPS facts help the driver: F1 shows the driven distance was 0.1 km shorter than the optimal route (17.1 vs 17.2 km), so there is no detour or out-of-the-way stop from which improper conduct could be inferred, and no RD-2 amount to refund.

I do not contest the profiles, but note the same facts (F6: 999 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days) mean there is no basis for a flag_account against the driver under RD-6, and profile facts cannot decide the case either way.
